A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeBias-CLIP research. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support comparison across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval experiments, ablations, caption-perturbation analyses and SDXL image-generation results, including appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds experiments investigating positional embeddings and token average pooling in Appendix E.2.

M1.justification: The default DeBias-CLIP augmentations, losses and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Appendix E.2 adds an experimental DeBias-CLIP variant that averages encoded text tokens instead of using EOT-based aggregation; this changes the tested variant's procedure without replacing the default method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ShareGPT4V training, the same short- and long-caption retrieval datasets, and SDXL generation evaluation. The new encoder experiments reuse DOCCI and existing sentence-permutation/removal scenarios rather than introducing new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: TULIP appears in standard retrieval comparisons in both versions, but v2 additionally evaluates TULIP ViT-L against Long-CLIP and DeBias-CLIP in the caption-perturbation comparison in Figure 9. The principal benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New Appendix E.2 introduces ViT-B Long-CLIP and DeBias-CLIP controls trained for three epochs with average pooling versus original token aggregation. It also applies the existing perturbation protocol to TULIP ViT-L. Existing benchmark splits, metrics and stated training settings are retained; revised scores alone do not establish changes to those settings.

E4.justification: Appendix E.2 and new Figures 9–10 test whether relative positional embeddings or average pooling alleviate early-token bias. These extend the existing robustness investigation with two architectural checks; earlier sampling, padding, training-duration and attention analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests for the compared experiments. The reporting practice remains point estimates and descriptive plots.

E6.justification: Table 4 revises DeBias-CLIP Flickr I2T scores from 57.0 to 56.6 for ViT-B and 65.1 to 64.8 for ViT-L. Tables 5 and 8 revise three-epoch Long-CLIP Urban1k/DOCCI T2I from 81.0/74.1 to 82.7/75.2; several appendix Flickr scores also change. Figures 9–10 add architectural-control results. Main long-retrieval Table 3 and image-generation Table 12 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The caption, sampling, loss and attention formulations in Equations 1–14 are retained. The new positional-embedding and pooling discussion introduces empirical tests, without new formal assumptions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: summary-first captions sustain positional bias, and DeBias-CLIP improves retrieval and robustness through caption augmentation without additional trainable parameters. Revised numerical margins do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix E.2 adds the interpretation that relative positional embeddings and average pooling do not by themselves resolve the observed bias, strengthening the rationale for addressing training captions. Existing limitations concerning summary-first benchmarks and relational understanding remain.

D1.justification: Appendix E.2 documents the new controls' pooling operation, ViT-B architecture and three-epoch training, plus the ViT-L configuration used for TULIP. The main hyperparameter table, caption-sampling pseudocode, hardware disclosure and code link are unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds SuperCLIP to Section 2.1 and the references. Appendix E.2 also expands the comparison with TULIP's rotary positional embeddings, positioning caption augmentation against architectural approaches to the bias problem.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized prose edits in related work, empirical motivation and method exposition, expands the Mila affiliation, and adds a supplementary-material heading and Appendix E.2. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds two appendix bar charts, relocates retained tables and attention plots, and separates the supplement from the references. Figure 2 changes the OpenAI legend label to CLIP. New Figures 9–10 have a caption inconsistency: they mention the first two sentences, whereas Appendix E.2 specifies swapping the first and fourth.

improvement.justification: The new architectural controls in Appendix E.2 address plausible alternative explanations for early-token bias and modestly strengthen the empirical argument. This gain is limited by unexplained revisions to reported scores and the new figures' inconsistent permutation captions. The core method, benchmark coverage and principal conclusions remain stable.
